question.text: An investor wants to compare two diversified equity schemes using a beta-based risk-adjusted performance measure. Which measure is MOST appropriate?

explanation.text: The Logic: Treynor ratio is a risk-adjusted performance measure that uses beta (systematic risk) in the denominator. The workbook states that Treynor comparisons should be restricted to diversified equity schemes, so it is the appropriate measure for comparing two such schemes. The Trap: Sharpe ratio uses standard deviation (total risk), not beta, so it does not match the beta-based framing of the question. Standard deviation alone is a risk measure, not a risk-adjusted performance measure, and absolute return ignores risk entirely. Note: The stem deliberately frames the comparison in terms of the beta-based, diversified-equity context that the workbook supports for Treynor, without relying on any R-squared screen.
